title: ui panels
shortDescription: A dungeon crawler's screen out of sprites: nine-slice windows that open and follow the canvas, portraits and counters packed at run time, a dialog typed out in a bitmap font — five draw calls
description:
A party screen in the look of Tiny Rogue, every piece of it a sprite.

**Nine-slice panels.** Windows, cards, slots, bars and the button are one kind on `gridBase({columns: 3, rows: 3})` with `NineSlice`: `setSliceFrame(frame, 'panel-stone')` takes the frame and its insets out of the slices of an Aseprite UI kit (`panels.aseprite.json`), and `sliceScale` keeps the border at its pixel size — a whole-number scale of the pixel art — however far `setSize()` stretches the middle. `Anchor` places each panel by a corner: the main window at its top left follows the canvas, the inventory opens from its top right corner, the dialog box grows upwards from its bottom left, and the HP bars are nine-slices whose length is the hit points. *style* gives the windows another panel of the kit, insets and all. See [Nine-slice panels](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/sprites.md#nine-slice-panels) and [A grid base](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/sprites.md#a-grid-base).

**DynamicAtlas.** The anime portraits are loaded as images and packed at run time into one `DynamicAtlas`, together with labels drawn by a callback — the names, and the HP and MP counters, which `redraw()` draws anew in place when the numbers change, without touching their sprites. One `FeatureSprites` draws all of them; a portrait flashes with `Flash` on a hit. See [Atlases built at run time](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/sprites.md#atlases-built-at-run-time-dynamicatlas).

**Bitmap text.** `BitmapFont.parse()` reads the `pixel-8` BMFont; `writeText()` writes the title, the quest and the dialog with word wrap at `maxWidth` and `align`, and the dialog is typed out letter by letter. `layoutText()` measures the tooltip of the inventory and draws the labels into the atlas. See [the text guide](https://github.com/spearwolf/twopoint5d/blob/main/packages/twopoint5d/docs/text.md).

The screen is drawn by an orthographic camera of a `Stage2D` in five draw calls — panels, icons, pictures, the panels over the icons, text. Hover the inventory, click *NEXT*, or *hit the party*.
